types.name: GaussianSplatComponent
types.doc:
A captured Gaussian splat scene (.gsplat, imported from a trained .ply or a
.splat file) placed in the level. Drawn into the HDR scene colour with the
rest of the world, sorted back to front on the GPU, one LOD level chosen
per frame from the camera distance.

members.name: lighting
members.doc:
0 = Captured: the colour is the radiance the capture saw, shown at the
brightness it was captured at whatever the scene exposure. 1 = Lit: the
colour is albedo, lit by the scene's sun and sky ambient with each
splat's flattest axis as its normal (no shadows received).

members.name: lodPixelError
members.doc:
How far a coarser LOD level's merge cell may project, in pixels, before
a finer level is drawn instead.

members.name: collision
members.doc:
0 = none, 1 = one convex hull around the opaque splats, 2 = boxes over
the occupied cells of a voxel grid (static, walkable).

members.name: cloud
members.doc:
The loaded cloud (an FGaussianSplatCloud), type-erased: SceneTypes sits
below the asset system. Shared, so a scene copy draws the same buffers.

members.name: color
members.doc: Common properties

members.name: intensity
members.doc:
Deliberately carries no MOWO_UNITS: what this number means is decided by
intensityUnits below, so a fixed suffix would be wrong for every value of
that enum but one.

members.name: intensityUnits
members.doc:
Photometric units for `intensity`. Legacy (default) keeps the historical
artist scale and the range-window falloff — every existing scene renders
byte-identically. Lumens/Candela/EV100 make a local light physical (true
inverse-square falloff, the radius only windows the cull range); Lux is
the directional-only illuminance unit. Mismatched unit/type combinations
fall back to Legacy semantics.

members.name: colorTemperature
members.doc:
Blackbody color temperature in Kelvin (0 = disabled, 1000-15000 valid).
Multiplies the authored color by the normalized Planckian-locus tint at
packet build — never per pixel.

members.name: radius
members.doc: Point/Spot light specific

members.name: sourceRadius
members.doc:
Area light source radius (R3 lighting upgrade). A physical emitter size
(a sphere/disk bulb) → soft, large specular highlights via the
representative-point method. 0 = a classic punctual light.

members.name: innerConeAngle
members.doc: Spot light specific

members.name: areaShape
members.doc:
Rect (area) light specific — emitter extents in world units. The emitter
faces along the entity's forward axis; width runs along the right axis.
Disc reads width as its diameter, tube reads width as its length and
height as its diameter.

members.name: contactShadowLength
members.doc:
Screen-space contact shadows — a short depth-buffer ray march toward the
light that grounds small-scale contact geometry the shadow map misses.
Ray length in world units; 0 = off (UE default). Applies to all types.

members.name: iesProfilePath
members.doc:
IES photometric profile — a real-world luminaire intensity distribution
(.ies file in the VFS, or a "builtin:*" preset). Empty = a uniform light.

members.name: cookieTexturePath
members.doc:
Light function / cookie (gobo) — a texture projected through the light
frustum that tints and masks the emitted light. Spot/rect project along
the aim axis; point lights map by direction. Empty = no cookie.

members.name: lightFunctionMaterialPath
members.doc:
Light function (UE's): a material — best a graph with Domain = Light
Function, whose Emissive becomes the filter — evaluated every frame and
projected through the light like the cookie, which it replaces. Point,
spot and rect lights; a directional light ignores it. Empty = none.

members.name: lightChannels
members.doc:
Light channel bitmask — a light only affects geometry whose own channel
mask shares a bit. Default 1 (channel 0) matches the default mesh mask, so
an unauthored scene is unchanged. 0 is treated as "all channels". Four
channels are enforced per pixel (bits 0..3); higher bits read as 0.

members.name: castShadows
members.doc:
Shadow casting. Default ON per the UE convention — MDF omits
default-valued fields, so unauthored scenes pick the new default up
and an explicit untick keeps working.

members.name: CreatePoint
members.signature: static LightComponent CreatePoint(const Vec3& col = Vec3(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f), float intens = 1.0f, float rad = 10.0f)

members.name: CreateDirectional
members.signature: static LightComponent CreateDirectional(const Vec3& col = Vec3(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f), float intens = 1.0f)

members.name: CreateSpot
members.signature: static LightComponent CreateSpot(const Vec3& col = Vec3(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f), float intens = 1.0f, float rad = 10.0f, float innerAngle = 25.0f, float outerAngle = 35.0f)

members.name: CreateRect
members.signature: static LightComponent CreateRect(const Vec3& col = Vec3(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f), float intens = 1.0f, float rad = 10.0f, float w = 1.0f, float h = 1.0f)

members.doc: Direction should be provided from transform

members.name: ToPointLight
members.doc: Position should be provided from transform

members.name: ToSpotLight
members.signature: SpotLight ToSpotLight(const Vec3& position, const Vec3& direction) const
members.doc: Position and direction should be provided from transform

members.name: ToRectLight
members.signature: RectLight ToRectLight(const Vec3& position, const Vec3& direction, const Vec3& rightAxis) const

types.name: MeshSubmesh
types.doc:
One submesh = one (mesh, material) pair within a multi-submesh model.
Imported FBX/glTF often have several submeshes (body, head, hair...) each
with its own material slot — every submesh is drawn as a separate draw call.
hasLocalTransform lets a submesh place a SHARED mesh at its own offset
under the entity (foliage tree instances) without duplicating vertices.

members.name: maxDrawDistance
members.doc:
0 = unlimited. When > 0, Scene::OnRender drops the submesh once the
camera is farther than this from its world position — foliage tree
meshes hand off to GPU impostor cards past r.Foliage.ImpostorDistance.

members.name: collisionOnly
members.doc:
A UBX_/USP_/UCP_/UCX_ piece: kept so slot indices and the collision
resolver still line up with the model, never drawn.

types.name: MeshRendererComponent
types.doc: Engine-level mesh renderer component for scene rendering

members.name: material
members.doc:
Primary submesh — kept as direct fields for primitives and back-compat.
For multi-submesh models, this is index 0. `material` is a VIEW: it may
point at an asset-owned material (ModelResource/MaterialAsset keep those
alive) or at an inline per-entity material, whose allocation lives in
`ownedMaterial` below.

members.name: ownedMaterial
members.doc:
Strong reference to an inline (non-asset) material. MaterialComponent
and MeshRenderer hold ONE object through it and the last component to
die frees it — with its GPU texture refs, exactly once — instead of
leaking it for the process lifetime. Null whenever `material` views an
asset-owned material: the asset holds that Ref and a reimport keeps the
object in place, so the view stays valid.

members.name: AdoptMaterial
members.doc: The view is set FROM the Ref, never the reverse (see MaterialComponent).

members.name: primaryLocalTransform
members.doc:
Node transform of the primary submesh (the source model's root axis/
unit correction lands here for flat model_path assignments). Identity
for primitives.

members.name: primaryCollisionOnly
members.doc: The primary submesh is a collision piece (see MeshSubmesh::collisionOnly).

members.name: additionalSubmeshes
members.doc: Submeshes beyond index 0 (empty for primitives / single-mesh imports).

members.name: modelPath
members.doc:
VFS path of the source model (empty for primitives).
Used for serialization round-trip through the Asset system.
Every inspector field carries a category: Details lays a component whose
fields are all categorised out as one section per category (Static Mesh,
Materials, Lighting, Rendering), the way UE shows a static mesh.

members.name: meshType
members.doc:
Primitive type name ("cube", "sphere", "cone", etc.) — empty for file-based meshes.
Used by runtime to create primitive meshes without editor resource cache.

members.name: modelNodeIndex
members.doc:
Index into the source model's node tree (ModelResource::GetNodes) when
this entity is one node of a model instantiated as a hierarchy (UE-style
FBX with several mesh objects). -1 = whole model on a single entity (the
flat default, back-compat). When >= 0 the resolver pulls ONLY that node's
submeshes and leaves their local transforms at identity — the node's own
placement lives in this entity's TransformComponent and the parent chain,
so the node transform must not be baked in a second time.

members.name: meshAsset
members.doc: Asset reference (non-empty when loaded from asset pipeline)

members.name: materialPath
members.doc:
Optional material-asset override (.mdfmat). When set, replaces the
material the model imported with for the PRIMARY submesh — this is how a
MaterialAsset / material instance gets dropped onto a mesh from the
editor (the inspector renders an asset slot for any MOWO_ASSET_REF
string field). Empty = use the model's own material. Lazy-resolved into
materialOverride at render time (Scene::OnRender), mirroring decals.
Hidden from the generic rows: Details edits it as Element 0 of the
Materials section, beside the model's other slots.

members.name: materialSlotPaths
members.doc:
Overrides for the model's further material slots: entry i replaces the
material of submesh i + 1 (slot 0 is materialPath). An empty entry keeps
the model's own material.

members.name: materialOverride
members.doc:
Resolved cache for materialPath (null until resolved; re-resolved when
materialPath changes). RUNTIME_ONLY — never serialized.

members.name: resolvedMaterialPath
members.doc: guards re-resolve

members.name: slotMaterialOverrides
members.doc: The same pair per further slot, sized with materialSlotPaths.

members.name: lightChannels
members.doc:
Light channel bitmask — the mesh is only lit by lights whose own channel
mask shares a bit. Default 1 (channel 0) matches the default light mask.
Enforced per pixel in the deferred pass: the low 4 bits ride the
G-Buffer's RT3.B low nibble. 0 means "all channels".

members.name: castShadows
members.doc:
Whether this mesh renders into shadow maps (CSM, local atlas, VSM).
Rides every DrawCommand the entity submits; the actor-level
MStaticMeshComponent mirrors its own castShadows into this field.

members.name: receiveShadows
members.doc:
Whether shadows fall ON this mesh. Rides the draw into the G-Buffer as
the RT3.B anisotropy sentinel (FLightChannels), so the deferred and
MegaLights passes skip every shadow term for its pixels — a first-person
weapon or a ground card that must not catch the world's shadows. The
trade is that an opted-out surface shades isotropically.

members.name: renderCustomDepth
members.doc:
UE's Render CustomDepth Pass / CustomDepth Stencil Value: the mesh also
rasterises into the custom depth target, depth-tested only against the
other opted-in meshes, with its stencil value in the R8 companion. A
post-process material reads both (Scene Depth / Custom Depth / Custom
Stencil nodes) — outlines, x-ray, "highlight the objective through the
wall" all key on this — and the CustomDepth / CustomStencil view modes
show them. Off by default: the targets are allocated on first use.

members.name: receiveDecals
members.doc:
UE's Receives Decals. Off, the mesh rasterises into the decal receiver
mask and every projector discards on its pixels — a character walking
through a scorch mark keeps its own surface.

members.name: castCapsuleShadows
members.doc:
UE's Cast Capsule Shadows (skeletal meshes only — a static mesh has no
bones to build capsules from): the posed skeleton casts soft capsule
occlusion on the sky light and a soft sun shadow, which is what grounds
a character the shadow map is too coarse to. The radius scale thickens
or thins every capsule (1 = a capsule about a fifth as thick as its bone is long).

members.name: IsApproxIdentity
members.doc:
True when a transform differs from identity by more than a small
epsilon — lets the flat-drop path skip the per-submesh multiply (and
keep AABB picking exact) for models whose node transform is identity
(legacy v1 .mmodel with no node tree, primitives).

members.name: AssignFromMeshAsset
members.doc:
Replace all submeshes from a loaded MeshAsset. Drops a model into the
primary slot + additional slots in one shot, so every submesh of the
imported model becomes visible.

members.name: ClearAdditionalSubmeshes
members.doc:
Drop only the multi-submesh data, leaving primary mesh/material in place.
Used when switching to a primitive or clearing a model assignment.

types.name: FPointCloudLayout
types.doc:
The chunk geometry every saved cloud is written against. A point stores its
position as three u16 offsets from its chunk's corner, so changing either
number after clouds exist on disk silently moves every point in them — a
change here is a file-format version bump and a converter, not a tuning pass.

members.name: kPageCapacity
members.doc:
One GPU page. Small enough that a sparse chunk costs little and that
eviction frees a predictable, modest amount; the pool is maxPoints /
kPageCapacity pages and a chunk takes a page per kPageCapacity points.

members.name: kMaxPagesPerChunk
members.doc:
A chunk's points are addressed by a u16 in the dedup table, so a chunk
past this is thinned rather than grown.

members.name: kMaxChunkPoints
members.signature: static constexpr uint32_t kMaxChunkPoints = kPageCapacity * kMaxPagesPerChunk

members.name: kPositionQuantum
members.doc:
65535 steps span the whole chunk, so a point exactly on the far face
still encodes without clamping and the error bound is half a step.

members.name: kBirthTicksPerSecond
members.doc:
Birth time is a u16 on a 0.05 s clock: a 10 Hz sweep still gives every
pulse its own stamp, and the ring wraps after ~55 minutes — far past the
longest fade a cloud can author, which leaves the expiry sweep a wide
band to catch a long-dark point before its stamp comes round.

types.name: FPointCloudSector
types.doc:
A world sector — one chunk. Chunking by sector is what makes the cloud
cullable, streamable, evictable and serializable in pieces, and it is what a
record's position is relative to — every one of those wants the same unit,
so there is only one.

members.name: kMaxCoordinate
members.doc: Past this a coordinate no longer fits its 21-bit key field.

members.name: Key
members.doc:
Each field masked to its 21 bits: unmasked, a negative coordinate's
sign extension ran into the fields above it and (0,-1,0) shared a key
with (0,-1,2) — harmless while points were stored in world space, fatal
once a record is decoded against the corner of the chunk it landed in.

members.name: IsAddressable
members.doc:
Finite and inside the keyable world, so FromPosition's float-to-int
conversion is defined and the key cannot alias.

types.name: PointCloudPoint
types.doc:
GPU point record, 16 bytes, read by PointCloud.hlsl as one uint4:
x | y<<16                     position, chunk-local, kPositionQuantum steps
z | octX<<16 | octY<<24       octahedral normal
birth | intensity<<16 | flags<<24
range:3 | material:4 | owner:3 | page:22
There is no colour. What a point looks like is derived in the shader from
range, material, owner, intensity and age, so recolouring the cloud — a
colour-blind palette, an owner tint — never touches a point.

members.name: WithoutPage
members.doc:
The page says where a record sits in this machine's GPU pool, which two
machines holding the same cloud assign differently; everything else is
the point itself.

members.name: QuantizeAxis
members.signature: static uint16_t QuantizeAxis(float world, float origin)
members.doc:
In double, from the world coordinate and the chunk corner, against the
exact step count: a float subtraction across the origin (-0.3 - -8) and
a float divide by the rounded quantum each push the error past the
half-step bound by a fraction of a percent.

members.name: EncodeOctahedral
members.signature: static void EncodeOctahedral(const Vec3& normal, uint8_t& outX, uint8_t& outY)
members.doc:
Octahedral: the unit sphere folded onto a square, eight bits a side. A
point needs its normal only for direction (the displacement along it,
the eye-dome term), and at this size the worst-case error is about a
degree and a half.

members.name: DecodeOctahedral
members.signature: static Vec3 DecodeOctahedral(uint8_t encodedX, uint8_t encodedY)

types.name: FPointCloudSample
types.doc:
A point as a caller has it: world space, with its normal and what it hit.
The accumulator is the only thing that turns one into a record, because the
record's position means nothing without the chunk the accumulator picks.

types.name: PointCloudDrawRange
types.doc:
A contiguous run of the points SSBO. Culling and LOD both reduce to "draw
fewer of these", so the accumulator hands the renderer ranges rather than a
point count and the renderer never learns what a chunk is. The origin is the
corner of the chunk every record in the run is relative to.

types.name: PointCloudDrawStyle
types.doc:
How one submission is rasterized. It exists because the persistent cloud and
the decaying half are drawn from the same buffer with the same pipeline but
must not look the same: an ephemeral point has to read as something that is
going away. Life is derived from each point's birth stamp and this
submission's clock, and this is the curve applied to it, so retuning the
fade is a push constant rather than a re-upload.

members.name: pointSize
members.doc:
Splat diameter in PIXELS. It is honoured on every backend because a
point is drawn as a screen-aligned quad: the per-vertex point-size
builtin this used to rely on exists only in SPIR-V, so a cloud
authored at 6 px rasterized at 1 px on all three of the other
backends and the size row read as broken.

members.name: fadeExponent
members.doc:
>1 holds the point at full opacity and then drops it late (a silhouette
that lingers and then is gone); 1 is a linear fade.

members.name: sizeFadeMin
members.doc:
Screen size at zero remaining life, as a fraction of pointSize. 1 keeps
the point the same size for its whole life.

members.name: splatRoundness
members.doc:
0 draws the splat as a square, 1 cuts it to a disc. Anything between
is the radius at which the corner is discarded.

members.name: ageNow
members.doc:
The submission's clock and lifetime, in the units its points' birth
stamps were written in (the persistent cloud's 0.05 s ticks, the
ephemeral ring's 60 Hz ticks). A lifetime of 0 draws every point at
full life. Lifetime is a uniform rather than baked per point, so
shortening it re-ages the whole cloud at once.

members.name: fadeHold
members.doc:
The three-phase curve over the point's age, as fractions of the
lifetime: full opacity until fadeHold, easing (by fadeExponent) down to
fadeFloor by fadeDissolve, then dissolving — each point dropped at a
stable, per-point moment — until nothing is left. The defaults are the
plain pow(life, exponent) curve the renderer always drew.

types.name: PointCloudSplat
types.doc:
One Gaussian splat grown from the accumulated scan, as PointSplat.hlsl reads
it, 64 bytes. The covariance travels as its three scaled principal axes
(Sigma = sum a a^T): the vertex stage projects each axis instead of building
a Jacobian, which needs the view-projection alone. The shade words are a
synthetic point record's z and w (birth/intensity, range/material/owner), so
a splat goes through the same palette, accessibility tables and age curve as
the points it grew from.

members.name: key
members.doc:
Stable per-splat hash: the dissolve key, so an ageing splat thins out at
the same moment every frame.

members.name: maxPoints
members.doc: it, never the other way round.

members.name: pointSize
members.doc: Splat diameter in pixels

members.name: splatRoundness
members.doc: 0 = square splat, 1 = disc

members.name: fadeEnabled
members.doc:
Age fade for the PERSISTENT cloud. A scanned surface that never dims
turns a scanner game into a lighting pass done once — the world stops
being dark and the scan stops being a decision. With this on, the
accumulator stamps every admitted point with the moment it was
revealed and the shader derives the point's remaining life from it, so
the fade costs no per-frame CPU work and no re-upload however large
the cloud gets.

members.name: fadeSeconds
members.doc:
How long a revealed point takes to reach its floor. Re-scanning the
same surface re-stamps the point, so the fade is a reason to keep
scanning rather than a punishment.

members.name: fadeSizeMin
members.doc:
Splat size at zero remaining life, as a fraction of Splat Size. Below 1
a dying point shrinks as well as dims, which reads as the surface going
away rather than as fog drawn over it.

members.name: fadeHold
members.doc:
The three phases of an aging point, as fractions of Fade Duration: it
holds full until Hold, eases down to Floor opacity by Dissolve, then
dissolves point by point — at a stable per-point moment, so it thins
rather than flickers — until the chunk is empty and its pages go back.

members.name: cloudPath
members.doc:
Where the accumulated cloud lives on disk. The points themselves are far
too large to sit in this component's MDF node, so the component persists
a path and the chunk stream persists beside the scene — the same shape
the nav-mesh companion file already uses. Without this a revealed world
is lost on every scene save, savegame and level transition.

members.name: ephemeralEnabled
members.doc:
The decaying half of a scan: points that landed on something that can
move. They are never admitted to the persistent cloud — they are wrong
the moment the body moves — and that wrongness is the beat the game is
built on, so the fade is authored here rather than hardcoded.

members.name: ephemeralCapacity
members.doc:
Extra SSBO capacity ON TOP of maxPoints, not a share of it: the ring
writes past the last sector page, so the persistent cloud keeps every
point it was budgeted. The lifetime that goes with it lives on
FPointCloudBudget beside the other accumulator numbers, and both are
retunable live through r.PointCloud.Ephemeral.Capacity / .Lifetime.

members.name: growSplats
members.doc:
Gaussian splats grown from the accumulated scan: every cell of the
persistent cloud the player has hit often enough fills in as one soft,
oriented splat under its points, and keeps growing in as the surface is
scanned again. Same palette and age curve as the points; the points stay
on top. Off by default — it changes the look of every scan.

members.name: splatGrowPoints
members.doc: Hits a cell needs before its splat reaches full opacity.

members.name: pointCount
members.doc: Runtime state (NOT serialized)

members.name: accumulator
members.doc:
The FPointCloudAccumulator that owns this cloud's points. Without one
there is nothing to draw: a record's position is relative to a chunk,
and only the accumulator knows which.

members.name: splatField
members.doc:
The FScanSplatField the bridge grows for this cloud (Grow Splats on).
Owned here, type-erased because the field lives in Game: the component
going away frees it, and a scene copy shares it rather than leaking one.

free.name: static_assert
free.signature: static_assert(sizeof(PointCloudPoint) == 16, "PointCloud.hlsl reads a point as one uint4")

types.name: ReflectionCaptureComponent
types.doc:
A local reflection capture: the scene rendered into a cubemap from this
entity and prefiltered into the same roughness-mip layout the sky IBL uses,
so surfaces inside the influence volume reflect the room they stand in
instead of the sky. Blended by influence with parallax correction; the sky
IBL fills whatever influence weight is left over.

members.name: blendDistance
members.doc:
Fraction of the influence volume spent fading out at its boundary, so
neighbouring captures cross-fade instead of popping.

members.name: recapture
members.doc:
Set to re-render the capture; the renderer clears it once the new
cubemap is prefiltered.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

members.name: skyRotation
members.doc:
Yaw of the environment about world up, in DEGREES (the editor unit for
every other rotation). It turns the visible cubemap sky and every lobe
derived from it together, so the sky you see and the sky you are lit by
stay one sky. A procedural atmosphere ignores it — its sun disc is
placed from the directional light's world direction, and yawing it would
slide the disc off the light that shades the scene.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: TextRenderComponent
types.doc:
UE's Text Render: a line (or lines) of text standing in the level as a flat
plane on the entity's XY axes, facing along its forward. The renderer
rasterises the string once per change and draws it as an in-scene quad that
geometry occludes, tinted by Color.

members.name: worldSize
members.doc: The height of one line of text in metres; the width follows the string.

members.name: horizontalAlignment
members.doc: Which point of the text block sits on the entity's origin.

members.name: texture
members.doc:
The rasterised string and what it was cut from: rebuilt when the text
changes, never serialized.

members.name: AlignmentOffset
members.signature: static Vec2 AlignmentOffset(ETextRenderHAlign horizontal, ETextRenderVAlign vertical, float aspect, float lines)
members.doc:
The text block's centre relative to the origin, in units of one line
height, for a block `aspect` lines wide and `lines` tall: Left puts the
origin on the left edge, Top on the top edge (Y up).

members.name: QuadLocalMatrix
members.signature: static Mat4 QuadLocalMatrix(ETextRenderHAlign horizontal, ETextRenderVAlign vertical, float aspect, float lines, float size)
members.doc:
The text quad in entity space. Forward is -Z, so a reader standing in
front looks along +Z and has -X on their right: the block is turned
half a turn about Y, or it reads mirrored from the front and correctly
only from behind.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

members.name: Custom
members.doc:
Shape and queries of a lake with no rendered surface — the gameplay-only
body UE calls Custom. Buoyancy, swim detection and the depth query all
answer inside it; nothing is drawn, so a hand-authored mesh or a decal
can stand in for the surface.

members.name: depth
members.doc:
Water column depth below the surface at this point. Feeds the depth
query and the terrain carve request; it does not move the surface.

members.name: velocity
members.doc:
Downstream speed at this point, m/s. 0 means "inherit the body's Flow
Speed" — the value every spline authored before per-point velocity
existed carries, so those rivers keep flowing at exactly the rate they
did.

members.name: oceanQuadTree
members.doc:
Ocean LOD. A fixed grid spends the same triangle on the horizon as on the
wave breaking at the camera, which is why the pre-quadtree ocean was
capped at a few hundred metres before the vertex count stopped being
affordable. Rivers and lakes keep their spline meshes — a ribbon and a
closed polygon are not grids.

members.name: oceanLodExtent
members.doc:
Side of the camera-following rendered patch, in metres. 0 = auto: the
whole body up to 1 km, past which the patch follows the viewer inside the
body's own extent. Never larger than Ocean Size — the query box is the
body, and a patch drawn outside it would be water nothing floats on.

members.name: waveSpectrumPath
members.doc:
Wave spectrum asset (.mwaves). When set it overrides the five inline
spectrum fields below; when empty they are authoritative.

members.name: spectrumWaveCount
members.doc:
0 = the legacy four-band curve every pre-spectrum scene was authored
against. Any positive count switches to the generator, on both the CPU
query and the vertex shader.

members.name: spectrumMode
members.doc:
0 = the geometric band falloff, 1 = Phillips, 2 = JONSWAP. The two
spectral modes take their band amplitudes from an energy density at each
band's wavenumber and stop reading Amplitude Falloff; Wind Speed drives
them instead.

members.name: spectrumCascadeCount
members.doc:
Patch sizes the bands are spread over, each a quarter of the one before.
One cascade is a single band of scales; three reach from the swell down to
the chop without spending sixteen bands inside one octave.

members.name: flowMapResolution
members.doc:
Painted flow map. A river gets its current from the spline tangent, but a
lake has no centreline to take one from, so its current is painted: a
square RG raster over the body's own XZ box, 128 meaning "no deflection on
this axis". Zero resolution = nothing painted, and the body flows exactly
as it did before the tool existed.

members.name: flowMapData
members.doc:
The raster itself, hex-encoded RG8. It is a string rather than a texture
asset because it is authored per body and has no life outside the scene
that owns it — a sidecar asset would need a UUID, a browser entry and a
delete-safety edge for something a designer thinks of as part of the lake.
Hidden from Details: a few thousand hex characters is not an editable row.

members.name: oceanDepth
members.doc:
Water column depth for a body with no per-point depth to read — the
ocean plane. Answers the depth query and nothing else.

members.name: priority
members.doc:
Which body wins where two overlap. A river crossing a lake reads as a
river when its priority is higher; equal priorities blend across the
shoreline band instead of one cutting the other off.

members.name: transitionWidth
members.doc:
Metres of this body's own shoreline over which it hands the surface over
to whatever it overlaps. Zero is the pre-transition behaviour — the higher
priority simply wins at its own edge, which is a step in the height and a
pop in buoyancy where a river meets a lake.

members.name: carveBankWidth
members.doc:
Metres beyond the water's edge over which the terrain carve ramps back to
the untouched heightfield. Too narrow and the river sits in a slot with
vertical walls; too wide and it flattens the valley it runs through.

members.name: flowMapBinary
members.doc:
The flow map decoded once into raw bytes. Held as a string because that is
what the reflection tables can carry; every query samples this and never
the hex, or a boat's four buoyancy probes would decode a hundred kilobytes
of text per frame.

members.name: flowMapDecodedFrom
members.doc:
The hex the cache above was decoded from. A length check alone would not
notice an UNDO: the editor's component snapshots restore flow_map_data and
skip runtime-only fields, so a reverted stroke leaves a map of the same
size with different bytes, and the queries would keep pushing boats along
a current the designer just took back.

members.name: waterDepth
members.doc:
Water column depth the info texture rasters under this plane. A plane has
no bed to measure, so this is what it declares; 0 means "never said" and
the shader keeps the screen-space thickness it always used.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

members.name: flow
members.doc:
Horizontal flow (m/s) of the sampled surface — non-zero only for rivers,
pointing downstream along the spline tangent. Buoyancy and character
water use it to push bodies along the current.

members.name: depth
members.doc:
Water column depth below the surface, in metres. Authored per spline
point (rivers), averaged over the polygon (lakes) or taken from Ocean
Depth. 0 means the body never said.

members.name: shoreDistance
members.doc: Distance to the nearest shoreline, metres. Large for an unbounded plane.

members.name: bodyId
members.doc:
Which body dominates here — the ECS entity id of the WaterBodyComponent
that won the transition, or 0 for the global WaterComponent plane. Audio
and gameplay key ambiences off it: a swimmer crossing from a river into a
lake is a different sound, and "which surface am I in" has no answer in
the height alone.

members.name: bodyWeight
members.doc:
How much of the dominant body the answer actually is, 0..1. Below 1 the
point sits in a transition band and the height, flow and depth above are
already the blend — this says so, so a caller crossfading an ambience
crossfades over the same band the surface does.

members.name: waveHeight
members.doc:
Wave excursion of the dominant surface at this point: the height minus
the body's still-water level. Positive on a crest, negative in a trough.

types.name: FWaterShoreSample
types.doc:
Where the water ends, and how far away that is. NearestShore answers against
the body that dominates the query, because the shoreline that matters to a
swimmer is the one belonging to the water they are in.

members.name: MakeBodyGerstnerParams
members.doc:
The one place a WaterBodyComponent becomes wave parameters. The renderer
and the query both go through it: two copies of this derivation is how
the surface that floats things drifts from the surface that is drawn.

members.name: SampleWaterSurface
members.signature: static FWaterSurfaceSample SampleWaterSurface(World& world, const Vec2& worldXZ)
members.doc:
Height/normal (and river flow) of the topmost water surface over worldXZ.
Considers both the global WaterComponent plane and spline
WaterBodyComponent bodies; the highest covering surface wins.

members.name: GetWaterHeightAt
members.signature: static bool GetWaterHeightAt(World& world, const Vec3& worldPosition, float& outHeight)
members.doc:
Gameplay entry points. These are what a boat, a swim volume, a footstep
surface query or a Visual Script graph should call — they hide the body walk and
the Gerstner inversion behind the four questions gameplay actually asks.

members.name: GetWaterDepthAt
members.signature: static float GetWaterDepthAt(World& world, const Vec3& worldPosition)

members.name: GetWaterVelocityAt
members.signature: static Vec3 GetWaterVelocityAt(World& world, const Vec3& worldPosition)

members.name: IsUnderwater
members.signature: static bool IsUnderwater(World& world, const Vec3& worldPosition)
members.doc:
True when worldPosition sits below the water surface covering it. The
renderer's underwater pass asks FWaterRenderState the same question
against the published frame state; this one answers off the ECS, so it
works on a dedicated server with no renderer at all.

members.name: SurfaceInfoAt
members.signature: static FWaterSurfaceSample SurfaceInfoAt(World& world, const Vec3& worldPosition)

members.name: NearestShore
members.signature: static FWaterShoreSample NearestShore(World& world, const Vec3& worldPosition)
members.doc:
Closest point on the shoreline of the body covering the query. Invalid
outside every body: "the nearest water's edge to a point on dry land"
would have to walk every body in the world, and nothing asks it.

members.name: TransitionWeight
members.signature: static float TransitionWeight(float shoreDistance, float transitionWidth)
members.doc:
How much of a body a query is, given how far inside its own shoreline the
query sits. A width of zero is the pre-transition rule — the body owns its
interior right up to its edge — and any positive width is a smooth
handover over that many metres.

Shared with the info-texture raster on purpose: the raster is a cache of
this function, and two handover rules would put the drawn seam somewhere
the buoyancy seam is not.

members.name: BlendTierWeights
members.signature: static void BlendTierWeights(const std::vector<float>& shoreDistances, const std::vector<float>& transitionWidths, const std::vector<int32_t>& priorities, std::vector<float>& outWeights)
members.doc:
Resolves a set of overlapping bodies into per-body shares that sum to one.

Priority tiers are walked from the top down and each tier claims the share
its strongest member is confident of: a body deep inside its own shoreline
claims everything and the lower tiers never speak, while one standing in
its own transition band leaves the rest of the answer to whatever it is
running into. With every width at zero this is the old rule exactly — the
top priority wins outright — so a scene that never touches Transition
Width is unmoved.

The gameplay query, the info raster and the per-vertex shading blend all
call THIS. Three copies of a handover rule is three places for the drawn
seam to end up somewhere the buoyancy seam is not.

members.name: FlowMapHalfSize
members.doc:
Half-side of the square a body's painted flow map covers, in body-local
metres. The paint tool, the info raster and the query all size the map
with this one call — three copies of "how big is the body" is how a
painted current ends up sampled at a different scale than it was drawn.

members.name: EnsureFlowMapDecoded
members.doc:
Decodes the hex flow map into the component's runtime byte buffer if it is
not already there. Cheap and idempotent: a size that already matches the
resolution is the whole test.

members.name: SampleFlowMap
members.signature: static Vec2 SampleFlowMap(const WaterBodyComponent& wb, const Vec2& localXZ)
members.doc:
The painted current at a body-local XZ, m/s. Zero when nothing is painted,
when the point is outside the map, or for a river (whose current is its
spline tangent and must not be overridden by a stroke).
